newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-KOEMAN AIMS TO END CAREER AT TOP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KOEMAN AIMS TO END CAREER AT TOP.

text.p: Ronald Koeman is on the final lap of a long and hugely successful professional soccer career.
The 33-year-old defender has much to look back on but hopes his swan-song will be a long-awaited Feyenoord championship.
The Rotterdam club trail league leaders PSV Eindhoven by a single point but have assembled a team that looks capable of going all the way to a first Dutch league title since 1993.
Koeman already has one Dutch title under his belt from the glorious 1988 season when his former club PSV Eindhoven captured both the domestic league and the European Cup.
In the same year he helped the Netherlands win the European Championship in Germany.
Koeman began his career as a teenager at Groningen, had a short spell at Ajax Amsterdam and three seasons with PSV before a six-year spell at Spanish champions Barcelona and finally Feyenoord.
Famed for his dead-ball play, varying from ferocious power to deft curling free-kicks, Koeman was always a great reader of the game, making up for a lack of pace.
One free-kick won the European Cup for Barcelona in 1992, the same year that another, controversial effort ended England's World Cup qualification dreams.
English fans reviled the Dutch defender for years as Koeman's crucial strike came moments after he escaped a red card for body-checking David Platt as he was clean through on goal.

One of a select band of stars to have won Europe's most prestigious trophy with different clubs, Koeman left Spain in the summer of 1995 to return to his native country to play out his career in Rotterdam.

The former international, who scored 14 goals in 78 matches for the Netherlands, almost quit at the start of this season after his plea for Feyenoord to bring in more top players fell on deaf ears. The club instead invested in the future, bringing in several young, inexperienced foreigners.

After threatening to hang up his boots prematurely, Koeman, dubbed "Snowflake" because of his blond hair and pale complexion, was persuaded to stay on and add experience to Feyenoord's European campaigns and the club's drive for the domestic crown.
Koeman is the central pivot for Feyenoord, playing just ahead of the three-man defence and prompting attacks with long, incisive passing.
His reading and understanding of the game at times give him the air of on-field coach as he cajoles those around him.
But even he is prone to the odd lapse.
When Feyenoord visited his former club Groningen last season, playing against his elder brother Erwin, Ronald scored the only goal of the game -- an own goal -- in the first minute.
He missed the first four games of the current league campaign after a stupid sending-off in the final fixture of last season.
After hanging up his playing boots, Koeman plans to attend courses and train to become a professional soccer coach.
